done_when: A review's fingerprint covers only the files the branch changes against its merge base plus the story doc or fix contract and the functional check, so merging an unrelated default-branch change keeps the review; a dismissal carries to a later review's finding with the same file and title; tests through forge close show both

findings.body: The new fingerprint keeps only each tree entry’s object ID, discarding its mode. After reviewing a branch that changes a script, removing that script’s executable bit leaves both the changed-path set and blob ID unchanged. If the functional-check text also stays unchanged, `forge close` reuses the review (`src/forge/close.py:66`), and the required PR check accepts it (`src/forge/prcheck.py:69`), despite the unreviewed change potentially breaking script execution. Include the tree entry’s mode alongside its object ID while retaining the changed-file scope.
findings.title: Preserve Git file modes in the scoped fingerprint

why: Merging the default branch into a task makes its clean review stale even when the task's own files did not change, and a new review raises findings that were already dismissed
